341.text: Soft inputs: every position after BOS replaced by the model's own concept token, which is what soft decoding actually feeds. 2.6501 against 2.6082, and this time the soft-trained model is ahead.

342.text: Store the pair and their difference. The gap is the quantity the curriculum is supposed to shrink, so it gets its own column instead of being left as mental arithmetic.

348.text: Read the two gaps, not the two best cells. The soft-input penalty falls from +0.2609 to +0.1384 nats, roughly a 47% reduction — the curriculum working as advertised, measured rather than asserted.

352.text: And it is not free: on hard inputs the soft-trained model is worse. It spent capacity learning to read blended embeddings and gave up some of its fit to clean ones, so the best single cell in the table is still standard-trained on hard inputs.

357.text: The honest shape of the result — robustness to soft inputs bought at a price on hard ones — and the conclusion left where it belongs: with whichever decoder you actually deploy.
